tldr: This stylized methods benchmark studies marginal selected-control ITE prediction in a saturated two-cell Lee model. A separated score tail of mass \(\lambda/n\) raises the randomized oracle length by exactly \(9\lambda/(8n)\). A total tail-count lottery is exactly finite-sample honest on the explicit global one-tail class and matches that expansion with an exponentially small oracle-relative remainder. For the same central score, a faithful instantiation of Lee\textquotesingle s published pooled adjusted-cutoff procedure has limiting length \(0.95\), compared with \(0.09\) for the count lottery; its atomic-tail incremental cost is \(9\lambda/(16n)\). The internal maximum-score allocator has a distinct positive Poisson length jump. Public fixed probabilities and exact score-shape restrictions define the benchmark; empirical applicability, unknown-composition two-scale inference, and sharp general minimax constants remain open.
gap: Lee identifies the ambiguity set and provides an adjusted pooled cutoff. Its specified central-score implementation does not exploit the public full-law two-cell coverage allocation studied here. Neither the inherited tail bound nor the published cutoff calculation supplies the exact globally honest count-spending construction with its rare-tail oracle expansion.
